slides.title: Questions you're too scared to Google

slides.q: What are the smelly white chunks I sometimes cough up?
slides.a: Those are probably tonsil stones, little clumps of food, mucus, and bacteria that harden in the pockets of your tonsils. They're usually harmless but can cause bad breath. Gargling salt water and brushing well help. Worth seeing a doctor if they keep coming back, cause pain, or one tonsil looks swollen.

slides.q: What's the little flap of skin under my tongue?
slides.a: Many people have small, fringe-like folds of skin on the underside of the tongue, called plica fimbriata. They're a normal leftover from development and completely harmless, even if you're only noticing them now. They don't need any treatment. Worth seeing a doctor if they become painful, swollen, or start to look different.

slides.q: Why do I get red bumps after waxing?
slides.a: Waxing pulls hair out from the root, and the follicles can get irritated and inflamed, causing small red bumps. They usually settle in a day or two. Skip tight clothes, heat, and touching the area right after. Gentle exfoliating a few days later helps prevent ingrown hairs. Worth seeing a doctor if bumps get painful or fill with pus.

slides.q: Why is my pee foamy sometimes?
slides.a: Occasional foamy pee usually just means you peed fast and hard, which whips air into it, or you're a bit dehydrated. That's harmless. Worth seeing a doctor if your pee is foamy every time, especially with swelling in your legs or face, since that can be a sign of protein in the urine.

slides.q: Why do I get pimples on my scalp?
slides.a: Scalp bumps are often folliculitis, which is irritated hair follicles, or regular breakouts from oil and product buildup. Sweat under hats, not rinsing shampoo fully, and heavy styling products can all play a part. Washing after workouts and switching products often helps. Worth seeing a doctor if they're painful, spreading, or causing bald patches.
